name: Acanthostachys pitcairnioides
description: Acanthostachys pitcairnioides is an epiphytic bromeliad native to tropical South America (Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina). It belongs to the Bromeliaceae family and forms a compact rosette of stiff, spiny, gray-green leaves (7-10 cm long), smaller than its relative A. strobilacea. The central tank (rosette) holds water and absorbs moisture. It produces small, inconspicuous flowers and reaches about 7-15 cm in height. In the wild it grows on tree trunks and branches in tropical forests. Ideal for terrariums and small enclosures due to its compact size.
careTips: Requires high humidity (60-80%) - ideal for terrariums
Bright indirect light - avoid direct sun
Keep central rosette (tank) filled with water - this is how it absorbs moisture
Well-draining epiphytic mix - orchid bark, sphagnum moss
Epiphytic - can be mounted on wood or grown in pots
After flowering, produces offsets (pups) that can be separated
Watch for scale insects and mealybugs
